- If sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is bearish (negative) in recent days, model often underestimates; adjust upward slightly to capture mean reversion or reversal.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overreacts and forecasts continued rise; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or apply lagged decay.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a smoothing filter or delay adjustment by 1–2 periods.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead), apply downward bias correction proportional to sentiment volatility.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to err on the side of overconfidence; use median of recent 3–5 day history as baseline for correction.
- For long-term (14+ day) forecasts, model often misses mean reversion; apply a 3–5 day moving average or trend-adjusted baseline to anchor forecast.
